title: Replication & Sharding
summary: Replication copies data for durability and read scale; sharding splits data for write/storage scale. Together they define how databases grow — and how consistency and operational complexity grow with them.

sections.title: Replication topologies
paragraphs: Primary-replica async replication is common: fast writes, possible loss on failover. Semi-sync and quorum replication reduce loss windows. Multi-primary increases conflict complexity.

sections.title: Sharding strategies
paragraphs: Hash, range, and directory-based sharding. Resharding is the expensive part — plan early. Cross-shard transactions should be rare.

sections.title: Read your writes
paragraphs: Async replicas cause stale reads. Session stickiness, primary reads for critical paths, or causal tokens mitigate.

sections.title: Ops realities
paragraphs: Failover automation, replica lag alerts, backup per shard, and schema change coordination dominate real-world success.

deepDive.title: Replication & Sharding — Operations
paragraphs: Operating Replication & Sharding in production means defining SLIs before tuning knobs, knowing amplification costs, and rehearsing failure modes.
Prefer reversible changes, feature flags, and canaries. Measure p50/p99 and error rate under load that matches production skew.
bullets: Define capacity from the scarcest resource
Keep rollback cheaper than forward repair when possible

deepDive.title: Replication & Sharding — Failure modes
paragraphs: Common failures around Replication & Sharding include overload, partial dependency outages, and silent correctness bugs that pass happy-path tests.
Inject faults in staging: latency, loss, clock skew, and disk full. Verify alerts fire and degradation is intentional.

expert.title: Replication & Sharding — Expert notes
paragraphs: At the expert level, Replication & Sharding intersects multi-region consistency, cost envelopes, and organizational constraints (team ownership, on-call load).
Write down the non-goals. Many outages come from optimizing a metric that was never the product requirement.

pitfalls: Reading replicas for strong consistency paths
whyItMatters: Database scale-out is where many systems hit a wall; these are the levers.
reflectionQuestions: What is your shard key — and what query cannot use it?
numbersToKnow: Know your p99 latency budget before adding hops
Peak load ≠ average load — plan headroom (often 2–3×)
Cross-region RTT is often ~50–150ms one way
